test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 25 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two trains, each 250 m in length, are running on parallel lines in opposite directions at speeds of 90 km/h and 60 km/h respectively. In how many seconds will they cross each other completely?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in **opposite direction** = 90 + 60 = 150 km/h.

Total distance to cover = Sum of **train lengths** = 250 + 250 = 500 m.

Time = 500 ÷ (150 × 5/18) = 500 × 18 ÷ 750.

Time = 2 × 18 ÷ 3 = 12 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 sec.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **Train 1** (L₁) = 250 m

Length of **Train 2** (L₂) = 250 m

Speed of **Train 1** (S₁) = 90 km/h

Speed of **Train 2** (S₂) = 60 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b25f143703a07be6b22eb88a167b3947413bd3ff6cebaa0106501e723249ac20.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂

Time = (Total Length) ÷ (Relative Speed)

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = L₁ + L₂ = 250 + 250 = 500 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 90 + 60 = 150 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 150 × (5/18) = 125/3 m/s

⇒ Time = 500 ÷ (125/3)

⇒ Time = (500 × 3) ÷ 125

⇒ Time = 4 × 3 = 12 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 12 sec.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When they move in the **same direction**, it is the **difference** (S₁ − S₂).

Total Distance for Crossing

When two trains cross each other completely, the **total distance** covered is always the **sum of their lengths**, regardless of the direction of travel.

Unit Conversion Shortcut

To convert **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/h**, multiply by 18/5.</p
